methodological_rigor.justification: The paper uses a rich time-course multi-omics design and includes orthogonal perturbations of RelA, NFKBIE, and SOX10, which gives the mechanistic claims some support. The main weakness is replication: several longitudinal RNA-seq and ATAC-seq series use one biological sample per time point, and some baseline epigenomic comparisons also rely on a single sample per cell line. The statistics are broadly reasonable for the assays shown, but the core temporal inference rests on limited replication and modeling rather than on a fully powered experimental design.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study, so the Oxford level is 5. The relevance is plausible rather than direct: it may inform future combination strategies for BRAF-mutant melanoma and potentially other MAPK-driven cancers, but the paper does not show patient-level benefit or prospective therapeutic validation.

reporting_quality.justification: No single reporting checklist applies cleanly to this multi-omic, mechanistic cancer study, so none is the best fit. The manuscript is method-rich and repeatedly notes source data, but the blinded text does not show an explicit data/code repository; reproducibility therefore depends on the detailed methods and supporting files rather than open deposition.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript's main novelty is the claim that drug-induced dedifferentiation proceeds through sequential transcriptional waves driven by NF-κB/RelA-dependent chromatin remodeling. That is a meaningful mechanistic advance over prior descriptions of persister states, but it is still an extension of known melanoma plasticity literature rather than a wholly new biological category.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is generally well organized, and the abstract gives a faithful high-level summary of the time-course, modeling, and mechanistic validation. The figure captions are detailed and numerically grounded, though the manuscript is dense and sometimes repeats the same mechanistic narrative across sections.

key_strengths: High-temporal-resolution multi-omics with orthogonal mechanistic perturbations.
A coherent model linking oxidative stress, RelA activation, and chromatin remodeling.
The story is extended across melanoma and two additional cancer models.
The writing and figure captions make the longitudinal logic easy to follow.
key_concerns: Several core time-course datasets use only one biological sample per time point.
A substantial part of the causal argument is built on correlation and modeling.
External validation is limited to a small number of patient biopsies and cell lines.
There is no explicit public data/code statement in the blinded text.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The paper is interesting and mechanistically coherent, but the limited replication in the longitudinal omics makes the evidence feel exploratory rather than fully settled, which keeps it in tier 3.
